question.leadin: This monarch put down Pugachev's Rebellion, and her lover Grigory Orlov helped orchestrate a coup to overthrow her husband, Peter III.
question.text: Name this empress of Russia known as "the Great."
question.answerHtml: Catherine the Great [or Catherine II; or Yekaterina Velikaya; or Yekaterina Alekseevna; or Princess Sophie of Anhalt-Zerbst]
question.clue: This ruler placed Stanislaw Poniatowski on the throne of a neighboring nation, and one advisor to this ruler created namesake sham villages on the Crimean peninsula.

swap.text: At the time of the Lenin Shipyards strike, Poland was part of the Warsaw Pact, an alliance led by what dissolved European country? This nation had leaders such as Mikhail Gorbachev and Josef Stalin.
swap.answerHtml: Soviet Union [or USSR or Union of Soviet Socialist Republics or CCCP or SSSR or Soyuz Sovetskikh Sotsialisticheskikh Respublik; prompt on Russia]
swap.clue: The Renovationist and Living Church movements in this country supported its longtime government, despite the newspaper Godless being published in this country by the state-supported League of Militant Atheists.

question.leadin: Name some leaders of the Soviet Union.
question.text: This successor to Stalin denounced him in a "Secret Speech" and instituted a namesake "thaw" where he released numerous political prisoners imprisoned by Stalin; the Cuban Missile Crisis occurred during his time leading the Soviet Union.
question.clue: During an American Exhibition within his country, this man debated then-Vice President Richard Nixon in a model kitchen.

swap.text: The House of Romanov came to an end with the Revolution of 1917, when this last Russian czar abdicated. The Bolsheviks killed still him and his family at the Ipatiev House.
swap.clue: This man's finance minister negotiated the end to a war with Japan in the Treaty of Portsmuth, and was named Sergei Witte.

question.text: The heirless death of Boris Godunov marked the beginning of this period of instability in Russian history, which saw the appearance of three False Dmitrys. The election of Michael Romanov as tsar ended this period.
question.clue: The eruption of a Peruvian volcano may have caused a massive famine during this period that included the Battle of Klushino.

swap.leadin: This event began when the offices of Rabochi Put were forced to close.
swap.text: Name this event which ended when the Aurora fired a blank shot to signal the capture of the Winter Palace. John Reed chronicled this event in his eyewitness account, Ten Days that Shook the World.
swap.answerHtml: October Revolution [or Bolshevik Revolution; prompt on November Revolution; prompt on Russian Revolution; do NOT accept or prompt on “February Revolution”]
swap.clue: Alexander Kerensky's cadets in Petrograd failed to hold the Winter Palace near the beginning of this event.

question.leadin: The history of a state centered on this city was related in the Primary Chronicle traditionally attributed to Nestor.
question.text: Yaroslav the Wise was once the grand prince of what city? Oleg of Novgorod founded a state named for this city that was ruled by the Rurikid dynasty.
question.clue: A ruler of this city militarily supported the Byzantine emperor Basil II, which resulted in the formation of the Varangian Guard, in exchange for marrying Basil II's sister Anna.

swap.leadin: This state was founded by Oleg of Novgorod and christianized by Vladimir the Great.
swap.text: Name this confederation ruled by the Rurik dynasty in modern-day Ukraine, often considered a predecessor to the Russian empire.
swap.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a historical figure.
question.text: This Ukrainian leader sought to reunite his homeland and so he turned against his former ally, Peter I, and joined Charles XII of Sweden. He was defeated at Poltava.
question.clue: This Cossack hetman and Ukrainian national hero. After he learned he was about to be replaced by Alexander Menshikov, this person defected during the Battle of Poltava.

swap.leadin: This man's father was the patriarch, Philaret, and he signed the Treaty of Stolbovo with Sweden in 1617.
swap.text: Identify this ruler who was elected by a zemsky sobor in 1613, founding a ruling house.

question.text: During the failed coup, this eventual leader called the coup "an attempt to crush Russia," and led the resistance against it in Moscow.
question.clue: Yegor Gaidar launched a failed economic program under this leader called "shock therapy."

swap.text: After an invasion of Livonia by this Russian ruler, Sweden formed a coalition with Poland and Lithuania to drive off the Russian incursion. Sweden was given modern-day Estonia from Livonia in the ensuing peace.
swap.answerHtml: Ivan IV Vasilyevich [Accept Ivan the Terrible or Ivan Grozny.]
swap.clue: Difficulties in his later years included a botched military campaign to retake western Slavic lands in the Livonian War, and the harsh government he created called the oprichnina, a far cry from his earlier Chosen Council.

question.text: This son of Basil III prosecuted the Livonian War and suppressed Novgorod. Ruling from 1547 to 1584, this Rurikid was notable for maintaining the oprichina, a secret police force, and being an all-around mean dude.
question.answerHtml: Ivan IV or Ivan the Terrible [prompt on partial answer]
question.answer: Ivan IV or Ivan the Terrible
question.clue: The Time of Troubles has its roots in the death of this infamous Russia ruler who according to legend blinded the architect of St. Basil's Cathedral.

swap.leadin: This ruler sent a letter to Ottoman sultan Abdulmejid I demanding the protection of Orthodox Christians traveling to the Holy Land in the lead-up to the Crimean War.
swap.text: Name this ruler, whose accession to the throne was opposed by Decembrists, who instead supported his brother Konstantin.

question.text: The first Ivan to rule Moscow acquired this byname after collecting the thrones of other cities as collateral on defaulted loans.

swap.leadin: The Valaam archipelago in this lake contains a 14th century monastery inhabited by Eastern Orthodox monks.
swap.text: Identify this lake, which receives water from Lake Saimaa via the rapids-filled Vuoski River and has a large outflow via the Neva River.
swap.clue: Unlike the Laurentian lakes, which are comparable to it in size, it is frozen during most of the winter, and important fisheries dependent on this body of water are located on the Svir river, which flows into it.

question.leadin: Name some things discussed in E. P. Thompson's The Making of the English Working Class, 9.
question.text: The preface mentions the English woman Joanna Southcott, who lef behind a wooden box of prophecies. Some crazy people later claimed the box foretold victory in this November 1854 battle during the Crimean War, known as the "Soldier's Battle." Menshikov's loss at this battle to Lord Raglan paved the way for the siege of Sevastopol.
question.clue: One general in this split his column of forces and passed one portion to FF von Mueller.

swap.clue: This 1921 rebellion of sailors from a namesake naval base.

question.text: A reduction in the required period of military service was introduced in 1874 by Dmitry Milyutin, who also organized an 1864 genocide targeting these people. The majority of the Egyptian Mamluks came from this group of oft-fetishized Caucasian Muslims.
question.clue: Authors like Christoph Meiners and Johann Friedrich Blumenbach popularized an anthropological classification named for this ethnic group.

swap.text: This Ukrainian anarchist incorporated his eponymous followers in to his Black Cross army, which initially allied with the Bolsheviks against the White Army, but soon turned against Bolshevik oppression and fought against them as well.
swap.clue: In the Ukraine, the Red and White Armies were opposed by the Black Army, which was led by this anarchist.
